summary: Giuseppe Bardelli (1815–1865) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien. He served as Dozent for Coptic and Sanskrit at the University of Pisa from circa 1845 to 1865.
Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti (1774–1849) was a linguist who studied at the University of Bologna from circa 1793 to 1797. He later held a post at the University of Bologna from circa 1797 to 1831.

Giuseppe Tucci (1894–1984) worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies, studying at Sapienza University of Rome, University of Calcutta, and Visva-Bharati University under Carlo Formichi, Giovanni Vacca, and Jikido Takasaki. He held posts at Calcutta, Sapienza, and ISMEO.

Giuseppe Vignato is a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who completed doctoral studies at Peking University in 2000 under Angela Falco Howard, Chongfeng Li, Su Bai, and Shichang Ma. He later held a post at Peking University.

Giyu Nishi (1897–1993) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Seishin Kato, Taiken Kimura, Hakuju Ui, Sylvain Lévi, Junjirō Takakusu, Masaharu Anesaki, and Makoto Nagai. He held posts at Tokyo and Toyo University.
Gnanawimala Chandima is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under the instruction of Uma Shankar Vyas.

Godabarish Mishra (1886–1956) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Ravenshaw College from circa 1906 to 1910 and the University of Calcutta from circa 1910 to 1912. He served as Director at the University of Madras until 2014.

Gombojab Tsybikov (1873–1930) was a Tibetologist and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Tomsk State University and Saint Petersburg State University. He served as Lecturer of the Mongolian Language at Far Eastern Federal University from circa 1906 to 1917.

Gopinath Kaviraj (1887–1976) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies who studied at the University of Allahabad (circa 1906–1910). He was Professor of Tantra-Śāstra at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from circa 1924 to 1937.

Gordon D. Kaufman (1925–2011) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Northwestern University and Yale Divinity School. He held a post at Harvard University from circa 1963 to 1995.

Gordon Johnson (born 1943) is an historian and Indologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, from circa 1961 to 1967. He later held a post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1974 to 2010.

Gottfried Hermann (1772–1848) was a linguist who studied at Leipzig University (circa 1786–1793) and the University of Jena (circa 1793–1794). He held a post at Leipzig University from circa 1798 until 1848.

Gottlieb Siegfried Bayer (1694–1738) studied at the University of Königsberg and under Christoph Theodosius Walther. He held posts at Königsberg, Kathedralschule zu Königsberg, and the Russian Academy of Sciences in ancient history and oriental languages (1726–1738).

Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner (1840–1899) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at King's College London in 1858. He held posts at King's College London in 1861 and at the Oriental Institute, Woking, from circa 1884 to 1899.

Govind Chandra Pande (1923–2011) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history. He served as Vice Chancellor at the University of Rajasthan (~1962–1977) and University of Allahabad (~1980–1984), and Chairman at Allahabad Museum and Indian Institute of Advanced Study (~1999–2004).

Govind Sadashiv Ghurye (1893–1983) studied Indology at Elphinstone College and completed a PhD at the University of Cambridge under W. H. R. Rivers (1922–1924). He held a post at the University of Mumbai from circa 1924 to 1959.
Govind Sakharam Kathavate was an Indology scholar who held the Sanskrit chair at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, succeeding Ramkrishna Gopal Bhandarkar.

Govind Swamirao Gai (1917–1995) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Chief Epigraphist for the Government of India (~1962–1976), Chief Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India (1966–1976), and Epigraphy Consultant for the American Institute of Indian Studies.
Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt was an Indologist who served as a Professor at Baroda College. He also held the post of Director at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, from circa 1950 to 1953.

Grace S. Fong (born 1948) is a sinologist who studied at McGill University and the University of British Columbia (until circa 1984). She served as Professor at Smith College (~1989–1992) and Department Chair and associate professor at McGill (~1992).
